text: April the fourteenth, nineteen twelve, just before midnight. The sea is flat calm, and there's no moon. The Titanic is doing about twenty-two knots, close to her top speed, through waters with ice warnings. A lookout spots an iceberg, dead ahead. By most accounts, around thirty-seven seconds before impact. The officer on watch orders the ship hard over, to steer around it, and signals the engine room. But a ship this big turns slowly. The bow swings left. Just not far enough.
